events.title: From the First Hackney Marsh Fun Festival to the last Hackney Carnival: An Exhibition to celebrate 50 years of Chats Palace
events.description:
Chats Palace will be showing unseen images from the first Hackney Marsh Fun Festival from 1974 alongside images from the last ever Hackney Carnival in 2024. Separated by fifty years the photographs have been taken by Hackney photographer Neil Martinson. 

The Hackney Marsh Fun Festival led to the creation of Chats Palace because the festival grew so large that its organisers desperately needed a permanent, year-round headquarters. In 1974, the old, Grade II-listed Homerton Library closed down when a newer library opened nearby. Rather than letting the building fall into disrepair or corporate hands, community activists and festival organisers marched on and occupied the building in 1976. They reclaimed it to ensure it stayed “for the betterment of East Londoners”. By 1977, they officially named it Chats Palace.

Once established, Chats Palace became the engine room for the festival, housing its carnival committee, building floats, hosting local pensioner clubs, and providing a legendary local stage for community theatre and music. 

The exhibition will be showing September and October 2026. For the duration of its stay, the Exhibition will be on display on Wednesdays, Thursday, Fridays, & Sundays from 11am-3pm.

events.title: Art Chat – The Bayeux Tapestry
events.description:
To celebrate the opening of the exhibition at the British Museum: Jo Cottrell and Michael Lewis ‘In Conversation’ on the Bayeux Tapestry

Jo Cottrell and Michael Lewis ‘In Conversation’ on the Bayeux Tapestry

To celebrate the opening of the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum, art historian Jo Cottrell and Michael Lewis, Curator, Bayeux Tapestry exhibition, British Museum will discuss this most famous embroidery. We will outline what this object is, who made it, when and why, before exploring its extraordinary story and incredible detail. After 30 minutes of insightful conversation about the object, its loan to the UK, and its display at the British Museum, the audience will be invited to ask any burning questions.

We hope you will join us!

The bar will be open until 10.30pm.

events.title: Join us at the Chats (Fun) Palace!
events.description:
We’ll be a part of the Fun Palaces weekend on Saturday 3rd October – with creative workshops, an exhibition celebrating local history, and our bar open for everyone to enjoy!

We will be open from 10 am – 4 pm, with tea / coffee, biscuits, and board games available. All workshops and the current exhibition on the day are free! Just grab your ticket here so we have a better idea of numbers, and get creative with us or hang out in our Library bar with friends and family 🎲

Schedule

  • In the morning (10:30 am – 12:30 pm), our friends at @change_act_theatre will be running an inclusive, relaxed introduction to the Theatre for Social Change approach, using drama games and participatory theatre exercises to explore experiences, communities, and social impact. Change, Act! Theatre are an experienced Disabled and Neurodivergent-led Applied Theatre company who co-create projects with local Disabled and Neurodivergent Communities and perspectives at the forefront.
  • In the afternoon (1 pm – 4 pm), Tristan from @londonzinescene will be facilitating a zine-making workshop incorporating digital culture and materials. There is an appetite for curating the unseen screenshots, photos, and image chaos that lurk on our devices. Zines allow for cognitive offloading and the ability to reveal ourselves and our digital world in a tactile way. Can we turn memes into zines to print and share? Participants will be able to use a free online ZINE MAKER app and portable printer. Tristan is a graphic designer and creative director with more than a decade in the creative industries, a recent fellow from Newspeak House, London College of Political Technology, and a member of faculty on the London School of Solarpunk.
  • Throughout the day, have a wander through our corridor and celebrate 50 years of Chats Palace’s history in the community. It features unseen images by local photographer Neil Martinson from the first Hackney Marsh Fun Festival in 1974 up to images from the last ever Hackney Carnival in 2024.

About FUN PALACES:
Fun Palaces is an ongoing campaign for community at the heart of culture and culture at the heart of every community. In 1961 the renowned theatre director Joan Littlewood and Cedric Price designed a Fun Palace building – a ‘laboratory of fun’. They imagined a building linked through technology to other spaces, accessible to those who wouldn’t normally go to arts venues or great centres of learning (which is the same concept that inspired the naming of Chats Palace!). Fun Palaces supports local people to co-create their own cultural and community events, across the UK and worldwide, sharing and celebrating the genius in everyone.
events.excerpt: We’ll be a part of the nationwide Fun Palaces weekend on Saturday 3rd October! Just turn up and get creative with us, or hang out in our Library bar with friends and family.

events.title: Hackney Folk Club presents: Bruce Molsky & Darol Anger
events.description:
Hackney Folk Club presents: Bruce Molsky & Darol Anger

Darol and Bruce have been musical explorers together for years, sharing a creative universe that’s resulted in some epic collaborations, crashing each other’s concerts and recordings, and just finding big joy in playing together.

Described as “an absolute master” (No Depression), Bruce’s take on tradition has landed him in collaborations with some of the world’s most highly respected players from roots to rock. His long association with Aly Bain and Jerry Douglas in the Transatlantic Sessions, his trio with Aly and Swedish maestro Ale Möller, and years of solo touring have landed him in the UK dozens of times. He is also a special guest on legend rocker Mark Knopfler’s CD, “Tracker.” Along with Andy Irvine & Donal Lunny, Bruce is a founding member of the supergroup Mozaik. The Grammy nominated Fiddlers 4, Darol, Bruce with Michael Doucet and Rushad Eggleston were at Fiddles On Fire in Gateshead.

Back home, Bruce and Darol tour extensively. Bruce also holds the title of “Visiting Scholar in the American Roots Music Program” at Berklee College of Music, where he is the go-to guy for the next generation of roots musicians.

Freestyle fiddler, composer, producer and educator, Darol Anger is at home in a number of musical genres, some of which he helped to invent. Exceptional among modern fiddlers for his versatility and depth, Anger has helped drive the evolution of the contemporary string band through his involvement with numerous pathbreaking ensembles such as his Republic Of Strings, the Turtle Island String Quartet, the David Grisman Quintet, The Montreux Band, his Duo with Mike Marshall, his current touring group Mr Sun, and others. He has performed and taught all over the world with musicians such as Dr. Billy Taylor, Bela Fleck, Bill Evans, Edgar Meyer, Bill Frisell, Tony Rice, Tim O’Brien, The Anonymous 4, Marin Alsop and the Cabrillo Orchestra, the Detroit Symphony, Bruce Molsky, Mark O’Connor, and Stephane Grappelli.

TIMINGS
Doors 7pm
Irish Trad Session: 7pm
Floorspots: 8pm
Bruce Molsky & Darol Anger: 9pm
Session in the Bar: 10-11pm

events.title: PRX.LIVE – Live Contemporary Music and World Premieres
events.description:
Following the blowout success of our sellout launch party at Folklore, contemporary music magazine PRXLUDES presents a night of music, conversations, and gatherings, celebrating today’s most cutting-edge composers.

Part live gig, part conversation, part social gathering: PRX.LIVE is a platform to gather people, share adventurous music and sounds, and start conversations about art, music, and the world in which we’re creating it.

Trailblazing ensemble Standard Issue premiere a new commission by rising-star composer Rebecca Galian Castello, alongside genre-defying works by today’s most cutting-edge early-career composers and live interviews from PRXLUDES hosts.

Hosted by PRXLUDES in partnership with ensemble Standard Issue and producers Stomping Ground. PRX.LIVE and Rebecca Galian Castello’s commission are generously supported by The Hinrichsen Foundation’s Multi-Year Partnership and Arts Council England.
Programme
Rebecca Galian Castello – Peach Fuzz (world premiere, PRXLUDES commission)
alongside other works by some of today’s most exciting composers – full programme to be announced!

What is PRXLUDES?
PRXLUDES is an online contemporary music magazine, platform, and resource dedicated to the promotion of the most cutting-edge contemporary music of today, with a focus on the work of emerging and early-career composers. The publication specialises in in-depth interviews with composers, ensembles, and organisations promoting the work of emerging artists. https://prxludes.net/

events.title: The Hackney Folk Club – Martha Tilston
events.description:
MARTHA TILSTON
“She has the power to draw an audience into her world, leaving all those present with a smile, and a few issues to ponder, too”-Time Out

With a pure silken voice and lyrics that inspire and captivate, Martha Tilstonhas developed a successful musical career with a large and loyal following.She has performed on some of the world’s most prestigious stages and festivals, recorded and released several critically acclaimed albums, gained a nomination for BBC best newcomer, appeared as a guest vocalist for Zero 7, toured internationally and worked with the some of the world’s most inspiring performers including Damien Rice, Nick Harper, KaeTempest, Roddy Frame (Aztec Camera) and Zero 7.

The past few years have seen Martha venture into the world of film making, gaining nominations for best arts film for The Clifftop Sessions and recently releasing her first feature film (with an accompanying Soundtrack Album) -The Tape -which is garnering much praise and excitement.With her long-time collaborators and musicians Matt Tweed and Matt Kelly, among others they entwine raw vocals, sparkling melodies and thought-provoking lyrics with filmic movements and earthy baselines. To see them live is to connect with longed-for parts of ourselves…

“Sharp, original songs that dissect the modern world. She captures both the harshness and enchantment of life”~The Guardian

events.title: Cabaret Roulette: Tarot
events.description:
Cabaret Roulette: Tarot

Cabaret Roulette takes eight of the highest calibre performers, gives them a brand new theme, and produces one extraordinary night of new cabaret.

Drag, circus, clown, burlesque, performance art… Artists representing the widest possible array of styles and disciplines are given two months to develop a new act on a single theme chosen in advance by you, the audience. Gamble is, the artists don’t know the theme until they agree to the show… and two months later we gather together to enjoy a night of bold risks, daring experiments, and chaotic cabaret debuts!

After our sold out success in August, the theme was selected and on Friday October 23rd we return to Chats Palace to do Tarot.

Expect fools, empresses, lovers, perhaps a cheeky devil or magician in the mix, as eight cabaret greats interpret the theme in their own creative ways.

Your tarot spread of performers will feature the magical talents of:

Cyro
Deeva D
Fempath
Joe Morose
Justin Elizabeth Sayre
Kheski Kobler
Miss Terri Boxx
Nat Funni
Plus pre-show tarot reading from the brilliant Jules McArthur of Twin Serpents Tarot!

Ticketing Info

General Admission – You know the drill, it gets you access to the show!

Solidarity Tickets – Able to make this show more accessible to others with financial barriers, as well as ensure the acts get as great a fee as possible, whilst also getting to see an amazing show? If you can afford to, please consider buying a solidarity ticket!

Pay What You Can Tickets – For anyone who wants them, no questions asked.

Doors to the auditorium will be at 7:30pm. Show will be 8:00pm until 10:30pm with two intervals. The bar is open from 6:30pm until midnight, so come along early, grab yourselves a drink, have a tarot reading, and mingle! Seating is unreserved, and the show will begin promptly, so arrive early to enjoy the bar and secure your spot!

events.title: Hackney Folk Club – Interstate Express
events.description:
Craig Judelman- Violin, vocals

Joe Buirski – Banjo

Jack B. Latimer – guitar, harmonica, vocals

With their high energy approach to traditional American songs and dance music, Interstate Express shares their love of old stories and passion for the joy of a fiddle tune that drives like a Mercedes on the open road.

The music that developed in America is as diverse as the people who brought it there, from fast banjo and fiddle dance tunes to folk songs, early country, blues and old ballads, this trio plays it all.

As comfortable on a festival stage as a sweaty bar, the band was formed on a long drive from Tennessee to New Orleans and is the newest project of fiddler and singer Craig Judelman, who learned from and performed with some of the great American traditional musicians of the last 50 years. Currently based in Berlin, he is bringing this legacy to European audiences, telling stories and sharing his American culture that goes much deeper than fast food and baseball.

events.description:
RITUAL: A Cabaret of Queer Journeys into Folklore.

This is a brand new variety night following the Celtic Wheel of the Year.

For our first outing, we greet you during Samhain.

Samhain marks the end of harvest season, on the cusp of darker half of the year. It is when the veil is thinnest between this world and the next. At the halfway point between autumn equinox and winter solstice, a gaggle of mystical performers will summon all things Samhain, folk, and ritual in what promises to be a bewitching night.

Pop down a bit earlier to enjoy some stalls, tarot, immersive experiences and treats (not tricks) before the cabaret at 8pm.

Doors and bar open at 6:30pm

events.title: CHATSlab: ClerknWell ARTslab goes to Chats Palace: John Hegley, Lorraine Bowen, Bob Karper, Lovell + More
events.description:
ClerknWell ARTSlab hops over to Hackney’s famous Chats Palace – just for one day – as these heroes of poetry, music and magic celebrate 50 years of Chats Palace Arts Centre.
This afternoon’s superChats:
John Hegley – ‘scandalously talented’ poet, singer and potato advocate.
Lorraine Bowen – started in the 80s in See You In Vegas playing bass guitar, through the 90s organising Women Performance Evenings, the 2000s performing in cabarets with John Hegley and eccentric acts and now post BGT coming back to Chats for a roost.
Ian Saville – Performers of the Indian Rope trick made a boy assistant disappear. Houdini made an elephant disappear. David Copperfield made the Statue of Liberty disappear. But Ian Saville has the much more ambitious goal of making International Capitalism and exploitation disappear. True, he hasn’t quite succeeded, but he keeps trying, and at the very least, he has made a lot of people laugh, and got some of them to think. A funny, magical, thought-provoking and topical celebration of Socialism.
Lovell – glorious lofi acoustic melodic grunge with razor-sharp charm.
Bob Karper – mixes true stories with documentary film, song, elements of live art and a variety of musical instruments, illustrating the idea that when examined closely, the everyday ordinary world reveals drama, art, tragedy, farce, magnificence.
Fran Isherwood – a poet with a comedic bent (bit like Housemaid’s Knee) known for flinging herself about on the London poetry circuit.
Diego Brown & the Good Fairy – the original twisted folk, and hosts of ClerknWell ARTSlab. Never knowingly over-prepared.
Bar open from 1pm, show from 2pm.

events.title: Who Poisoned the Salt Fish Fritter?
events.description:
WHO POISONED THE SALT FISH FRITTER – JAMAICAN NIGERIAN DETECTIVE DUO RETURNS!
Get ready for a wild ride with everybody’s favourite detective pair: Sherlock Holmes, Kiss-Me-Neck and Dr Watson To-Back-Side back on the case!
This time, they’re diving into a mystery that’s got everyone talking: who the hell poisoned Lord Seymour with the salt fish fritter? Expect twists, ridiculous physical comedy, and a whole lot of Caribbean flavour packed into one unforgettable night.

**What’s It About?**
A fresh, African Caribbean spin on classic whodunits. Our sharp-witted duo uncovers shady dealings, forgotten Black British history, and some seriously shady Victorian secrets—all while rocking killer costumes with island flair.
PG- Every penny goes back into making the show bigger and better.
**What Makes It Special:**
– A soundtrack mashing up old-school Caribbean beats with fresh vibes
– Slapstick comedy that’ll have you wheezing
– Victorian fashion… but make it tropical
– Eye-popping projected backdrops
– Dance scenes blending Caribbean tradition with street swagger

**Why It Matters:**
This isn’t just fun—it’s history you weren’t taught. The show digs into:
– Black British entrepreneurs way back in the 1700s-1800s
– How folks fought back against racism (with style)
– Lost stories that deserve to be remembered
– The living, breathing art of Caribbean storytelling
Come for the mystery, stay for the vibes. You won’t forget this one.

Doors Open: 6:00pm
Tickets 2-for-1 or £25 each
events.excerpt: This wild romp throws you into the 17th and 18th centuries, shining a light on the vibrant, innovative Black communities that history tried to erase. Packed with slapstick comedy, killer tunes, and twists so ridiculous, you’ll be laughing till it hurts

events.title: Hackney Folk Club – AK Patterson
events.description:
AK Patterson is a London-based singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist whose music blends gritty honesty with haunting beauty. Known for her unflinching exploration of dark and complex themes, Patterson crafts songs that find hope in the bleakest corners of human experience.

Described by fans as “Buckley with boobs” (in reference to Jeff Buckley), she prefers to label her style as modern chamber pop fused with the melancholic spirit of 90s Lilith Fair.

Acclaimed actor and musician Johnny Flynn included her in The Guardian’s cultural highlights of 2023 after attending her performance at the Brunel Museum and Guy Garvey on BBC radio said her track The Parting Grace was “a bit special”.

Patterson has also garnered attention for her collaborations with renowned drummer Adam Betts (Colossal Squid), known for his work with Squarepusher, Goldie, and Jarvis Cocker, and has contributed to Johnny Flynn and Sivu’s latest records.

Patterson reflects on her evolving sound: “These new songs may seem darker than ever, but they are ultimately about survival, resilience, and, above all, hope.”
events.excerpt: AK Patterson is a London-based singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist whose music blends gritty honesty with haunting beauty. Known for her unflinching exploration of dark and complex themes, Patterson crafts songs that find hope in the bleakest corners of human experience.

events.title: Hackney Folk Club – Anna McLuckie
events.description: Anna McLuckie is a Scottish singer, songwriter and Clàrsach player. Raised on classical and traditional music, Anna’s writing draws on her musical beginnings and also takes influence from her love of popular music and more experimental sounds. Her music sits in a world of contemporary folklore; her songs layered with interweaving harmonies, story led lyricism and free form structures. Based in London, she has performed in places around the world from Rockwood Music Hall NYC, to a concert series in Russia, to house shows and folk sessions. She’s appeared at festivals across the UK and supported the likes of Jake Xerxes, Fussell, Rozi Plain and Richard Hawley.

events.title: MIKE VIOLA
events.description:
West Hampstead Arts Club presents:

MIKE VIOLA

A rare opportunity to catch the great Mike Viola at the grand surroundings of Chats Palace.

Mike Viola. You probably already know him .. producer, songwriter, the kind of musician your favourite musicians quietly obsess over. Decades in, and somehow he keeps finding new generations to infect. Since 2019, he’s been on a proper run .. The American Egypt, Godmuffin, Paul McCarthy .. all cut at his LA home studio, Barebones.

Sold out US shows, a whole new fanbase, the usual. Then September 2024 brought Rock of Boston, recorded on half-inch tape over the winter of 2023, with Jake Sinclair on bass and Brendon Urie on drums. Viola wrote most of it on a Panic! At The Disco tour bus, between soundcheck and showtime, sneaking into whatever local studio he could find on his days off. When the tour ended, he and the band just carried on playing, no gap, no breath, just straight from hockey arenas into the tape machine.

Which might explain why the riffs feel bigger. On 12th November 2026, he brings that to London’s CHATS PALACE. No hyperbole necessary. Just go !
events.excerpt: Mike Viola. You probably already know him .. producer, songwriter, the kind of musician your favourite musicians quietly obsess over. Decades in, and somehow he keeps finding new generations to infect. Since 2019, he’s been on a proper run .. The American Egypt, Godmuffin, Paul McCarthy .. all cut at his LA home studio, Barebones.

events.title: HELD BY TREES
events.description:
HELD BY TREES

Not many bands carry the living DNA of their influences like Held By Trees. Their debut album Solace (April 2022) featured eight Talk Talk/Mark Hollis alumni plus veterans of Pink Floyd, Dire Straits, Blur and Eric Bibb. It drew wide critical acclaim, support from Guy Garvey and Stuart Maconie on BBC 6 Music and play on Radio 3, and charted at #4 on the Official Indie Chart and #23 on Physical Sales. The fledgling project earned press and media support.

The live band includes guitar legend Robbie McIntosh (McCartney, Pretenders, Talk Talk), Laurence Pendrous (keyboards), Paul Beavis (drums, The Waterboys), and Andy Panayi (flute/sax). After their live debut in October 2022, they recorded two EPs at Peter Gabriel’s Real World Studios: live tracks from Solace and new music Eventide (summer 2023). In 2024, Held By Trees collaborated with vocalist Martin Smith on the 13-minute epic ‘Lay Your Troubles Down’ and an EP (released autumn 2024), followed by a short tour.

Their second album Hinterland (April 2025) features musicians from Supergrass, Slowdive, Swans, Band of Susans, Primal Scream, Wire, My Bloody Valentine, returning Talk Talk alumni and Mark Hollis’ son Charlie. Hinterland has garnered widespread reviews from Uncut, RNR, Fireworks, The Daily Express, Prog Magazine, Magic Magazine (France) and online blogs. Press highlights: Mojo gave Solace 3/4 stars, praising ‘massive fuzz guitars’; Elizabeth Alker of BBC Radio 3 noted its ‘sparse but slightly proggy’ appeal; Record Collector called them ‘new heroes of prog/post-rock’; Classic Pop rated Solace 4.5/5 stars for fans of Hollis’s aesthetic.

June 9th, July 14th, August 4th, September 22nd, October 20th, November 17th

3 ticket price-points according to income (no questions asked)

“I loved the sonic and sensual journey that Jon created, and the qigong we did at the beginning to get our energy moving” Jacob

events.title: Hackney Folk Club: Chris Wood
events.description:
Hackney Folk Club Presents

Chris Wood

“… at art school they said I had a remarkable eye for trivia, like it was a bad thing.”

Reflections on minor league football, empty nest syndrome, learning to swim, Cook-in Sauce and of course, the Gecko as a metaphor for contemporary society!

Tom Robinson and Chris Difford are fans while Stick In The Wheel and The Unthanks look to him as an influence. In a world of soundbites and distractions Chris Wood is a truth seeker. His writing is permeated with love and wry intelligence, uplifting and challenging as he celebrates the sheer one-thing-after-anotherness of life.

Winner of 6 BBC Folk Awards, he’s played with The Royal Shakespeare Company and was a key member of The Imagined Village along with Billy Bragg, Martin and Eliza Carthy. A wise and soulful craftsman, his concerts are a cliche free zone.

events.title: Swell Maps, 14 Iced Bears & holr
events.description:
Swell Maps – recently reformed English experimental DIY, early punk and post-punk group originally between 1972 and 1980.

Led by ex-Chats Chair & arts contributor, Steve Bird (Jowe Head).

14 Iced Bears – British indie pop band associated with the C86 music scene. Formed in Brighton in 1985, by Robert Sekula and Nick Emery the band featured a shifting line-up of musicians across their seven-year existence, centred on songwriter and vocalist Rob Sekula and guitarist/songwriter Kevin Canham.

holr – holr (4-piece experimental post-rock ensemble) caustic-resonant, afterimage-patient ensemble architectures draw long-toned acoustic remainder from the algorithmic fault line. sectional & durational: a sea of glass. double bass / drums / electric guitar / electronics

events.title: The Magic Lantern’s Festival of Feeling: London
events.description:
The Magic Lantern’s Festival of Feeling: London

A one day ‘Festival of Feeling’ exploring the unique ability of songs to make sense of the limitless depth of our shared human experience. I have invited some of my favourite songwriters and musicians to share their songs and collaborate with me on some of mine. Performing in the beautiful and historic Chats Palace in Homerton.

Doors open at 3pm with live music in the bar. Sets in the main venue will start at 4pm with a 20 minute break between each act. During this time there will be live music in the bar. Music will finish at 10pm with the bar open afterwards.

Featuring performances from:

The Magic Lantern (full band)

Blythe

Sam Brookes

Fred Thomas & Lucine Musaelian

Samantha Whates

Quiet Folk

Zac Gvi & Wes Gibbons

And a whole bunch of special guests some of whom I can name later and some of whom you’ll just have to wait and see…..!

Concessions

We do not check your right to a concession or name your price ticket. If you feel you can afford the full price please select this ticket. However, concessions prices are there to help anybody attend the show – if you need a lower cost ticket you are in the best position to determine that. No questions asked.

Venue & Accessibility Information

There is step-free access into the building and the ground floor of the venue is fully wheelchair accessible, with double doors throughout and a dedicated disabled toilet.

For ticketed events, we offer a Personal Assistant/Companion ticket at no additional cost for every full-price patron ticket purchased by a customer who could not attend without the support of a PA/Companion, subject to availability at time of booking. Prior notice of the request for a Personal Assistant/Companion ticket is essential due to venue capacity.

The Magic Lantern’s ‘Festival of Feeling’ event will have unreserved standing although we can offer a preferred space for wheelchair users and customers who require a seat. If you would like to use this area, please contact the Front of House Team in advance of the event and we will reserve a place for you.

events.title: Hackney Folk Club – Tom Moore Quartet
events.description: Norfolk-raised multi-instrumentalist and producer Tom Moore brings his new quartet to the stage for 2026. Joined by Nina Harries (double bass), Oren McLoughlin (drums), and Charlie Wheatley (harmonium), the ensemble reimagines historic English folk melodies through a widescreen, cinematic lens. Moore—whose playing has been praised as “ingenious” by The Guardian—intertwines valve-amp electric guitar and viola with dark, atmospheric drones and a heavy, groove-driven rhythm section. It is an ensemble of creative players with the technical freedom to tear this material apart and reshape it live on stage—a raw, direct vehicle for Moore’s own playing. The result is a striking balance between early music textures and modern, deep-pocket acoustic arrangements.

events.title: Hackney Folk Club – Kris Drever & Cahalen Morrison
events.description:
Kris Drever & Cahalen Morrison

Kris and Cahalen are the ultimate ‘musician’s musicians’ who draw from diverse musical backgrounds but are friends and kindred spirits in their subtle instrumental mastery, evocative songwriting and innovative musicality.

Both have carved out a unique place and voice at the intersection of traditional folk and modern acoustic music, digging deep into the well of tradition – those of Scotland and America respectively – whilst pushing the boundaries of intelligent and poignant contemporary songwriting.

Kris Drever is among Scotland’s most acclaimed and distinctive contemporary musicians, celebrated for his warm voice, virtuosically expressive guitar playing and imaginative songwriting. Raised in the Orkney Islands, Drever is a renowned innovator as a solo artist and as one third of the award-winning trio Lau.

Now resident in Scotland, but hailing from the high desert of Northern New Mexico, Cahalen Morrison is equally at home on guitar, banjo, mandolin, is a captivating singer, whether in three-part harmony or unaccompanied, and an insightful and poetic wordsmith and songwriter.

Both artists will be releasing powerful new albums in 2026: Kris’ Doing this for love and Cahalen’s The Broken Bell.
